name: Weaver-ant fish
summary: A Rơ Măm dish of minced stream fish set under a weaver-ant nest so the ants’ secretion works on the meat. Both the tourism authority and VietnamNet say wait about half an hour, then fold in ant eggs and eat it with forest leaves.
origin: The Vietnam National Authority of Tourism and VietnamNet both name cá gỏi kiến vàng as a Rơ Măm dish of Kon Tum.
taste: VietnamNet says the fish is sweet and fragrant against the sour of young weaver ants, and hot from the leaves. The tourism authority describes the same ant secretion cooking the fish.
howToEat: Clean a large stream fish, take off the bone and skin, and mince it with lemongrass and chili. Set the bowl under a weaver-ant nest and shake the branch so the ants fall in. They bite the fish and secrete a fluid. The tourism authority says about 30 minutes. VietnamNet says half an hour. Then mix in cleaned ant eggs. Eat it with herb leaves or sung leaves.
A price, a street, and a clock were not printed on either article. Check on arrival.
where: With Rơ Măm communities in Kon Tum, on both articles. A city address was not printed. Check on arrival.
